occupations.cat: Refuse workers and other elementary workers

n.story:
Your role is transitioning from a mobile data collector to a specialized field technician and anomaly investigator. As smart meters and computer vision (OCR) take over the repetitive task of recording numbers, your daily route will no longer be defined by a list of addresses to visit, but by a list of 'exceptions' flagged by AI. You will spend less time behind the wheel and more time investigating complex issues that sensors cannot solve alone.

When you do arrive on-site, your focus shifts toward high-level diagnostics. Instead of just reading a dial, you will use AI-powered visual tools to identify subtle signs of corrosion or sophisticated tampering that automated systems have flagged as suspicious. Your value lies in your physical presence and tactile judgment—performing the 'last mile' of utility maintenance that requires human dexterity and the ability to navigate unpredictable physical environments.
auto: Manual recording of gas, water, and electricity digits
Route planning and GPS navigation between standard sites
Data entry and reporting of routine meter readings
Basic identification of visible meter faults
amp: Advanced corrosion and structural integrity recognition
Detection of sophisticated physical tampering and bypasses
Complex mathematical modeling for usage anomaly verification
tools: Predictive routing and logistics optimization platforms
n.adv: Focus on developing technical skills in utility infrastructure maintenance and learn to use digital diagnostic tools; your future value is in being a 'smart' technician rather than a data recorder.

n.story:
Your daily routine is being transformed from a fixed-route manual labor job into a data-driven logistics and security operation. Previously, you spent a significant portion of your week driving pre-set routes and manually checking stock levels. Now, AI-driven predictive analytics determine your optimal path in real-time based on live inventory data, traffic patterns, and even local event schedules. Tasks like adjusting temperature gauges and logging task records have moved entirely to the background, managed by IoT sensors and automated systems.

With the time saved on logistics, your role expands into a more critical oversight capacity. You are now a field technician who uses AI-powered surveillance to ensure public safety around machine clusters and a brand ambassador who ensures food hygiene standards are met through tech-assisted monitoring. You no longer just 'fill machines'; you manage a fleet of smart retail points, focusing on high-level maintenance and ensuring the security and satisfaction of the public in the spaces your machines occupy.
amp: Enhanced public safety monitoring via AI analytics
tools: Computer vision for security and stock rotation
n.adv: Shift your focus toward basic technical maintenance and data literacy; understanding the 'why' behind the AI's route and stock suggestions will make you an essential fleet manager.
